title: French Fries in the Oven
description: How to make oven-baked fries without a deep-fryer? In David Lebovitz’s My Paris Kitchen, he shows us a method that’s simple to do and a lot less messy. Of course, the baked fries are healthier with less fat involved. The trick to make crispy baked fries is by soaking the cut potato sticks in water for an hour. Then brown them thoroughly in a 400°F oven. Here is a new and improved process. Each and every step ensures that the baked fries come out crispy and light. Given the favorable results, I think it’s worthwhile to go through all the steps.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons sea salt or kosher salt
Fresh herbs, such as a big handful of sage leaves, a few sprigs rosemary or thyme, or a mixture of them
directions: No need to peel the potatoes, leaving on a few strips of skin as you go.
Cut the potatoes into 1/3-inch-thick (1cm) slices. Lay the slices on a cutting board and slice them into 1/3-inch-wide (1cm) sticks.
Put them in a large bowl with very cold, lightly salted water, and let them sit for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with the pan in the oven, with a silicon pad if you have one.
Drain the potatoes and lay them on a kitchen towel. Rub them with the towel to dry them very well.
In a bowl, drizzle potatoes liberally with olive oil and a sprinkling of salt and pepper and fresh (or dried, if necessary) herbs. Coat the potatoes evenly and gently, preferably with your hands.
Place potatoes onto the preheated pan, then arrange the fries in a single layer.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, rotating the pans from front to back and top to bottom midway during baking.
As they bake, stir the potatoes several times so they cook evenly.
Once the fries are golden brown and crispy, remove the pans from the oven and serve.
